verdictSummary: Heptabase's solo core is compact: build a local-first visual knowledge mapping app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on polish, sync, importers.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local-first visual knowledge mapping app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
whyPeopleStillPay: Heptabase: People pay for a writing surface they trust for years, plus migration tools, sync, and tiny interaction details that disappear into habit.
ongoingBurden: Own schema migrations, backups, sync conflicts, export compatibility, and long-term file readability.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Documents and an infinite canvas in one local-first app, without the research tax.

facts.install: Use AFFiNE Cloud or install the desktop app; self-hosted collaboration uses the official Docker Compose stack with AFFiNE, PostgreSQL, and Redis
facts.engines: AFFiNE AI supports bring-your-own-key routes for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and FAL; local storage is available in the desktop app, while self-host AI is configured server-side
facts.dataFormat: A local-only desktop workspace stays on that device; AFFiNE Cloud stores it in AFFiNE's service, while self-hosted workspaces use PostgreSQL for structured data, mounted blob storage for uploads, Redis for cache, and local configuration files
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers documents and an infinite canvas, but its canvas is less specialized for research cards, spatial synthesis, and guided sense-making than Heptabase's.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app is straightforward, but free self-hosted sync and collaboration require Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, persistent volumes, configuration, migrations, backups, and a correctly exposed server URL

alternatives.name: Logseq
alternatives.desc: Cards, block links and whiteboards for sense-making, with rougher furniture.

facts.install: Download the desktop/mobile release or use the hosted web app; no server is required for a local graph
facts.dataFormat: Classic file graphs are folders of Markdown or Org-mode files plus Logseq configuration/cache files and can be synced with a file service; the newer DB graph stores the graph in a local SQLite database, while optional Logseq Sync/RTC sends graph data to Logseq's service
facts.gapVsPaid: Its links and whiteboards are powerful, but whiteboard polish, mobile experience, and performance are rougher, while the newer database path still carries beta risk.
facts.setupBlocker: Stable local installation is simple, but the visually stronger DB graph/RTC path is still beta or alpha and explicitly carries data-loss warnings; free cross-device file-graph sync requires choosing and safely operating a third-party file-sync method

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.desc: Canvas boards backed by linked Markdown files and an enormous plugin drawer.

facts.install: Install the native Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, or Android app; no account is required for local use
facts.dataFormat: Ordinary Markdown files and attachments in a user-chosen local vault folder, with app settings and plugins under `.obsidian`; optional paid Obsidian Sync stores end-to-end-encrypted replicas in Obsidian's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: Canvas supplies free-form boards, but it lacks Heptabase's purpose-built card workflow, research structure, and guided visual knowledge experience.

notes: Strong page because Heptabase separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Heptabase.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local-first visual knowledge mapping app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: conflict-safe multi-device sync; mature importers and exporters; collaborative editing and sharing.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
